name: Gāyatrī Mantra
source: Ṛgveda 3.62.10, prefixed with ॐ and the three vyāhṛtis
devanagari:
ॐ भूर्भुवः स्वः
तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं
भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि
धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात्
transliteration:
oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ
tat savitur vareṇyaṃ
bhargo devasya dhīmahi
dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt

translations.label: Translation — after S. Radhakrishnan (1953)
translations.text: We meditate on the adorable glory of the radiant sun; may She inspire our intelligence.

word_meanings.meaning: of Savitṛ, the impelling sun (genitive of savitṛ)
most excellent, to be chosen, desirable
may we meditate on, may we hold (1st person plural middle)

notes: ॐ and भूर्भुवः स्वः are the mahāvyāhṛti prefix — the three worlds — added in later ritual use; the three lines after it are the Ṛgvedic verse proper, addressed to Savitṛ in the gāyatrī metre the mantra is named for (three octosyllabic lines). Also called the Sāvitrī mantra. In the last line धियः + यः shows visarga sandhi: -aḥ → -o before a voiced sound, giving धियो यो. The verse's own grammar is masculine — यः and प्रचोदयात् refer back to सवितुः देवस्य — so translations render it "he"; the feminine "She" above follows the later devotional identification of the mantra with the goddess Gāyatrī, Veda-mātā, the Mother of the Vedas.
